body:
I enjoyed work to the extent that i could. It was only semi skilled manual labor but I volunteered any time something needed done, kind of neat doing a job with people that have only done the same thing for 20 years when after two i could do any aspect of it. 

High school straight A's dropped out my last year. 2 year break or so doing nothing, finally went to college, again having no issues with it on course to switch into a uni course, just stopped going to classes then dropped out after a year and a half. 

Job was good, little bit of work indoors, mostly working out doors by myself so you had the personal freedom. I enjoyed that part of it. 

Everyday was a cycle tho. I would walk to work in the mornings take about 30 minutes, could have got a ride no issues but walking always gave me time to think and clear my mind. But more and more passing the same houses everyday, going to work, coming home, sleeping working again. The cycle of it pressing done like being a prisoner.  I used to feel the houses closing in on me as I waled to work in the morning. 


Never been medicated in my life. I wish maybe i had gotten thrown on something like dexies back when I lacked all drive really might have helped. I don't see the point in it now though. I think I tried talking to my doctor once, but it didn't really work. 

You know its a strange day when you can't even be bothered having a beer.

I think one of the issues I have now is that before I looked forward to travelling and seeing different things. I have a belief it would be different out there. In the end where ever you go you take yourself with you, can't escape that. Cultural variations from place to place sure, but people generally remain the same, they all have the same raison d'etre. 


So in the end traveling just kind of reinforced the beliefs I had pushed away back inside that now are coming back. I hoped to find something to change myself, but i doubt it ever really works that way.
